stem: A client with newly diagnosed cancer has missed two appointments because of transportation problems and says, 'I do not understand which specialist I am supposed to see next.' Which action best reflects the role of the oncology nurse navigator?

options.A: Assess the client's barriers and understanding, coordinate with the interprofessional team, provide education, and connect the client with appropriate resources to support timely care.
options.B: Independently select the client's cancer treatment regimen and change specialist referrals without consulting the treating clinicians.
options.C: Limit involvement to entering appointment dates into the schedule because addressing transportation and care barriers is outside the navigator role.
options.D: Delay navigation until active treatment begins because nurse navigation does not apply during diagnosis and transition into treatment.

rationale: Current ONS/AONN+ guidance describes the oncology nurse navigator as an RN with oncology-specific knowledge who provides individualized assistance to help patients and caregivers overcome healthcare-system barriers. Navigation includes assessment, education, resources, coordination with the interprofessional team, support for informed decision-making, and facilitation of timely access to health and psychosocial care across the cancer trajectory, including diagnosis and treatment transitions. The navigator does not independently prescribe the oncology treatment plan and the role is broader than administrative scheduling.
educational_objective: Apply the oncology nurse navigator role to a client with barriers to timely cancer care by prioritizing assessment, education, interprofessional coordination, and resource linkage within RN scope.
source_organization: Oncology Nursing Society (ONS) and Academy of Oncology Nurse & Patient Navigators (AONN+)
source_document_title: Role of the Oncology Nurse Navigator Throughout the Cancer Trajectory; Oncology Navigation Standards of Professional Practice
source_version_date: Joint position statement approved 2025-02; professional standards published 2022-06
source_locator: 2025 joint position statement — definition of ONN and position bullets on transitions, barriers, interprofessional teams, education/resources; 2022 Standards — definitions of clinical navigator/oncology nurse navigator and oncology navigation
source_claim_supported: ONS/AONN+ states that oncology nurse navigators use oncology-specific nursing knowledge to assess and address healthcare-system barriers, provide education and resources, support informed decision-making, coordinate with interprofessional teams, and facilitate timely access to care throughout the cancer trajectory.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Management of Care — collaboration with the interdisciplinary team, continuity of care, referrals, resource use, and client care coordination
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — interdisciplinary oncology care coordination and navigation
correction_summary: Upgraded the original definition-only oncology nurse navigator item into an applied care-coordination scenario. Replaced the generic ONS homepage with the current 2025 ONS/AONN+ joint position statement plus navigation standards, clarified RN scope boundaries, and tested identification of barriers, education, resource linkage, and interprofessional coordination rather than rote role recognition.
audit_findings: Original item was a low-discrimination role-definition question with vague distractors rather than an applied nursing judgment item.

The February 2025 ONS/AONN+ position statement directly supports navigation across diagnosis, treatment, survivorship and end-of-life care, including removal of barriers and interprofessional coordination.
The final item preserves RN scope by excluding independent prescribing or unilateral alteration of the oncology treatment plan.
Distractors now represent concrete role-boundary and care-coordination errors rather than obviously dismissive statements.
Independent adversarial review found one uniquely correct response with no ambiguity, second answer, cueing, or unresolved scope conflict.
